'''Leticia González Herrero''' (born 17 March 1971) is a Spanish theoretical chemist, known for her work on molecular excited states, especially ultrafast dynamics of DNA nucleobases<ref>{{cite journal | author = Martin Richter, Philipp Marquetand, Jesús González-Vázquez, Ignacio Sola, Leticia González | title = Femtosecond intersystem crossing in the DNA nucleobase cytosine | journal = J. Phys. Chem. Lett. | year = 2012 | volume = 3 | issue = 21| pages = 3090–3095 | doi = 10.1021/jz301312h| pmid = 26296011 | last2 = Marquetand | last3 = GonzáLez-Vázquez | last4 = Sola | last5 = GonzáLez | arxiv = 2103.13070 | s2cid = 207548928 }}</ref> and highly accurate simulations of transition metal complexes.<ref>{{cite journal |author1=Michael Jäger |author2=Leon Freitag |author3=Leticia González | title = Using computational chemistry to design Ru photosensitizers with directional charge transfer | journal = Coord. Chem. Rev. | year = 2015 | volume = 304 | pages = 146–165 | doi = 10.1016/j.ccr.2015.03.019}}</ref>

==Biography==
Leticia González was born in [[Madrid]], where she studied [[chemistry]] from 1989 to 1994 at the [[Autonomous University of Madrid]]. In 1995, she earned her master's degree from [[King's College London]]. She returned to [[Autonomous University of Madrid]] for her [[PhD]], which she earned in 1998.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.uam.es/departamentos/ciencias/quimica/estruct/thesis.htm | title = PhD thesis in the group of M. Yáñez and O. Mó | access-date = 2016-03-08 | archive-date = 2017-02-15 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20170215232912/http://www.uam.es/departamentos/ciencias/quimica/estruct/thesis.htm | url-status = dead }}</ref> She then moved to the [[Free University of Berlin]] and completed her [[Habilitation]] in 2004.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://userpage.chemie.fu-berlin.de/~manzwww/main/group/theses.html | title = Thesis in the group of J. Manz | date = 9 October 2013 | access-date = 2016-03-08}}</ref>
In 2007, she was appointed Professor for Theoretical and Physical Chemistry at the [[University of Jena]]. In 2011, she became Full Professor for Computational Chemistry, Theoretical Chemistry and 
Scientific Computing at the [[University of Vienna]].<ref>{{cite web | url = https://medienportal.univie.ac.at/uniview/professuren/cv/artikel/univ-prof-dr-leticia-gonzalez/ | title = Media portal of the University of Vienna, new professorships in October 2011 | access-date = 2016-03-08}}</ref>

==Honours and awards==
* 2018: [[Doctor Honoris Causa]] of the University of Lorraine<ref>{{cite web | url = http://factuel.univ-lorraine.fr/node/9730 | title = Media portal of the University of Lorraine | date = 13 November 2018 | access-date = 2018-11-18 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PeEDdDteHBc | title = Youtube Video of the Doctor Honoris Causa Ceremony | website = [[YouTube]] | date = 14 November 2018 | access-date = 2018-11-18 }}</ref> 
* 2014: [[Löwdin]] lecturer
* 2011: [[Dirac Medal (WATOC)|Dirac Medal]] of the WATOC (World Association of Theoretical Chemists)
* 2006: Heisenberg Stipendium, [[Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft]] (DFG)
* 2005: Guest Professorship Award, Berliner Frauenförderung 
* 2005: SIGMA-ALDRICH Award for best Young Researchers, Spanish Royal Society of Chemistry, Spain  
* 1999: Alexander von Humboldt Fellowship 
* 1999: Premio Extraordinario de Doctorado 1998/1999 (Best PhD Thesis year 1998/1999), Faculty of Sciences, Universidad Autónoma de Madrid
